parsed.explanation: Combined regime has no general criminalisation of trans presentation and retains functioning courts, injunctions, litigation and local service protections, but a visitor faces operative universal exposures: binary federal passport/entry screening with refusal and possible fraud ineligibility, a federal government-facility ban, and a nationally attached facility ban in this division despite no local ban. Federal custody hormone removal and reported immigration-custody abuse add severe tail risk. Local protection is explicitly overridable nationally, so it does not cancel these exposures.

entry_documents.exposure: Federal binary sex definition; X markers halted for new US passports, existing valid to expiry; 2025 cable directs refusal where documents cast reasonable doubt on sex and consideration of lifetime fraud ineligibility for wilful misrepresentation. Passport confiscation/blocking reported.
entry_documents.protection: Fraud finding is not automatic, requires four elements, limited waivers possible. Several foreign governments issued advisories; civil-liberties suit pending, though Supreme Court allowed marker restriction in Nov 2025.
entry_documents.interaction: Document discrepancy at entry can escalate to refusal, investigation, detention and birth-sex placement, and stranded-document consequences abroad.

investigation_detention_custody.exposure: National corrections bureau from 2026 adopts hair cutting, hormone removal and psychiatric substitution for trans inmates; immigration custody reports forced labour, beatings, solitary and severe sexual abuse of trans men.
investigation_detention_custody.protection: Not documented. No jurisdiction-specific local custody conditions in inventory.
investigation_detention_custody.interaction: Entry fraud allegation or facilities trespass can lead to detention where hormone denial and misgendered placement are documented nationally.

federal_state_facilities.exposure: Executive order bars trans people from government-funded single-sex facilities congruent with identity. This division has no local bathroom ban, but national legislature attached a ban; activists protesting it were arrested 5 Dec 2024. Scope/buildings and visitor application not specified.
federal_state_facilities.protection: 29 states, 4 units and capital district have no ban in mapped categories; this division's local law has none and is on July 2026 low-risk list, with caution about national override.
federal_state_facilities.interaction: Local protection cannot repeal national ban; traveller must use federal/government facilities under birth-sex rule regardless of local stance.

care_services.exposure: Care for minors already banned in 27 states; Oct 2025 proposed national rules would bar public insurance reimbursement under 18; Jan 2025 order frames minor care as mutilation. Hormone removal in custody documented.
care_services.protection: Several orders blocked or enjoined; scope for adult visitors not documented. Not documented.
care_services.interaction: Emergency or continuation care in federal facilities may interact with birth-sex facility and custody rules; adult visitor care access remains uncertain.

threat_framing_law_enforcement.exposure: National justice reward memo uses 'radical gender ideology' among violent-extremist viewpoints; May 2026 counterterrorism strategy prioritises 'radically pro-transgender' violent secular groups. Four states make certain bathroom use criminal via trespass; one arrest March 2025, held 24h in men's ward.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.protection: Hate crimes punishable nationally by gender identity; employment discrimination prohibited under 2020 ruling. Local trespass example is other state, not this division.
threat_framing_law_enforcement.interaction: Threat framing raises police scrutiny, but dossier does not document routine street sweeps of visitors in this division.

minors_guardians.exposure: Jan 2025 order directs investigation of schools for 'gender ideology' and criminal prosecution of teachers facilitating a trans minor's social transition, including names/pronouns. Care bans in 27 states strand travelling families for under-18 care/insurance.
minors_guardians.protection: Several orders blocked/enjoined; no division-specific minor visitor protection documented.
minors_guardians.interaction: A travelling minor using school/federal facilities faces birth-sex rules and potential investigation of facilitators; guardian cannot rely on local law against national action.

street_violence_police_response.exposure: Not documented. No jurisdiction-specific local police practice in inventory; national poll shows majority support birth-sex documents/athlete rules, indicating social hostility risk but not visitor violence rate.
street_violence_police_response.protection: National hate-crime statute covers gender identity; 22 states plus capital district outlaw gender-identity discrimination. Local enforcement not documented.
street_violence_police_response.interaction: Absence of local violence evidence is not safety; national threat framing may affect police response if called.

remedies_unknowns.exposure: Passport suit unresolved; Supreme Court allowed restriction; facility ban remedy locally unavailable because national legislature controls division. July 2026 low-risk assessment method, local hate-crime enforcement, custody and ban scope are not verifiable.
remedies_unknowns.protection: Courts have blocked/enjoined several orders; legal-aid FAQ exists; local government remains elected though subject to national override.
remedies_unknowns.interaction: Remedies are partial and uneven: litigation may restrain some executive actions but does not remove in-force passport and federal-facility rules.

anchor_checks.comparison: Lower than this case: 0.35-A has birth-sex toilets in every public building with courts routinely rejecting complaints and no effective relief. Here bans are mainly government/federal, many states have none, this division has no local ban, courts have enjoined some orders, and no routine police extortion of visitors is documented. Similar universal-exposure tier, but narrower scope and working partial recourse raise it above 0.35.

Similar to this case: 0.45-A has birth-sex rule in all publicly funded buildings, upheld despite challenges, polite public, no presentation offence, one prosecuted assault. Here federal government-funded ban plus nationally attached division ban, passport/entry fraud risk and custody hormone removal match that unremedied universal-exposure level, offset partly by enjoined orders and local protections.

Lower than this case: 0.65-A has no trans-specific border or facility restriction, passports including nonbinary markers accepted, refusals corrected by office orders, attackers convicted. Here binary passport rule, entry discrepancy refusal/fraud exposure, federal facility ban and documented custody abuse are operative and not shown corrected, so cannot reach reduced-risk tier.

parsed.synthesis: The traveller encounters one system: local law is comparatively protective and no local bathroom ban exists, but national law directly governs this seat, imposes binary documents and federal facility exclusion, attaches its own ban, and controls custody, entry fraud, schools and minor-care funding. Functioning courts and injunctions mitigate some executive actions, and no organised visitor targeting, presentation imprisonment or death penalty is documented. The decisive exposures are in-force universal document/facility rules and severe custody practices, with unlockable local override. That places it at the lower elevated-risk anchor, not the 0.35 organised/unremedied-all-public-buildings tier nor 0.65 reduced-risk tier.
